prompt: A single wide illustration shows a brightly lit American hall of the Clay Mathematics Institute whose seven central pedestals display unsolved mathematical formulas, each tagged with a one-million-dollar prize, while a spotlight falls only on them and many equally famous problems remain in the dim outer shadows to show they are an incentive rather than a ranking; in the foreground a claimant waves a manuscript amid a press of journalists and rival mathematicians scrambling for credit, yet a seated institute panel with gavel and hourglass waits for publication and communal checking, visually separating mere announcement from official acceptance; beside them computer consoles and an AI figure co-author a proof whose speech-bubbles ask who counts as author, what machine involvement must be disclosed, and how the community can referee an argument no unaided human wrote.
